# javaabu/stats

> Time series and categorical stats for Laravel. A stat is a class (CountStatsRepository, SumStatsRepository, CountCategoricalStatsRepository, SumCategoricalStatsRepository) registered under a metric name with TimeSeriesStats::register() or CategoricalStats::register(). Chart builders (TimeSeriesChart, CategoryChart, PieChart, Sparkline, StatTile) turn metrics into charts, drawn as SVG with Onu's tokens in Blade (<x-stats::chart>) and with Onu's chart components in React (<StatsChart> from @javaabu/stats, shipped through javaabu/manifest). Charts can plot several stats or periods and compare with the previous period, and are cached with warming and invalidation. Route::stats() gives stats pages (stencil forms, javaabu/filters filters, CSV export) in Blade or Inertia React; Route::statsApi() gives a JSON API. Dates are grouped on MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL and SQLite. Viewing needs view_stats (javaabu/permissions, StatsPolicy).

Paths are relative to this file. In a project, that's vendor/javaabu/stats/.

## Rules

- Define stats as classes extending the package's repositories; never write your own `GROUP BY DATE(...)`/`YEARWEEK()` queries or fill empty days yourself. Generate them with `php artisan stats:time-series Name Model [--type=sum]` or `php artisan stats:categorical Name Model CategoryModel category_id`.
- Register every stat under a snake_case metric (`TimeSeriesStats::register(['payments_count' => PaymentsCount::class])` in a service provider, or `config('stats.time_series_stats')`), and refer to it by that metric in charts and requests.
- Show stats with the chart builders: `TimeSeriesChart::make('payments_count')->range(PresetDateRanges::LAST_30_DAYS)->mode(TimeSeriesModes::DAY)->compare()`. Render them with `<x-stats::chart :chart="$chart" />` in Blade, or pass them as Inertia props to `<StatsChart chart={chart} />`. Don't fetch the JSON API to draw charts in JavaScript, and don't add Chart.js.
- Several stats on one plot: `->stats([...])`; one stat over several periods: `->periods([...])`; against the previous period: `->compare()`.
- KPI tiles: `StatTile::make('metric')->compare()->sparkline()` in `<x-stats::stat-tiles>` / `<x-stats::stat-tile :tile>`, or `<StatsTile tile={…} />`.
- Charts are cached (10 minutes for periods that include today, a day for past ones). Register dashboard charts with `Stats::warm(fn () => [...])` and schedule `WarmStatsCache` or `php artisan stats:warm`; invalidate with `Stats::forget('metric')` or the `InvalidatesStats` model trait. Use `->withoutCache()` in tests that change data after building a chart.
- Filters: `StatsFilter::exact()`, `scope()` and `closure()` read `filters[...]`; `StatsFilter::from(SelectFilter::make('status')->options(...))` (javaabu/filters) adds a field to the stats form and reads its own query parameter. Don't name a filter after a stats parameter (`metric`, `mode`, `date_from`, …).
- Register routes yourself: `Route::stats(['prefix' => 'admin/stats', 'name' => 'admin.stats', 'guard' => 'web_admin'])` and `Route::statsApi([...])`. Never assume the `web` guard or `App\Models\User`.
- Dates are `CarbonInterface` (`CarbonImmutable` in apps that call `Date::use(CarbonImmutable::class)`): type-hint `CarbonInterface` in your own date ranges and stat overrides, and use the return value of `addDay()`, `startOfDay()` and the like.
- Authorize through `$stat->canView($user)` / the gate (`view_stats`, `StatsPolicy`); override the policy with `config('stats.policy')` or `Gate::policy()`. Run `php artisan permissions:sync`.
- For one model's stats, extend `TimeSeriesStatsController` or `CategoricalStatsController` and return fixed filters from `filters(Request $request)`.
- User-facing strings go through `__()`; stat names come from `getName()`. Use logical CSS (`ms-`, `pe-`) in published views; charts mirror in Dhivehi.
